subject: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>; legal@evergreenhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Kim — thanks for the call this morning. Attached is the clean order form we discussed and our latest DPA marked with the small transfers addendum (Evergreen_DPA_markedup_v3.docx). High level asks from your side: confirm whether Eden (your data team) will accept processor-only evidence or if you need controller-to-controller routing for EU traffic.

Quick notes / asks for legal: 
- We flagged the SCCs exhibit (section 4) — we propose using the EU Commission standard clauses + our hosting routing addendum.
- Roles: our suggested mapping is in the marked-up DPA (processor/subprocessor table). Please flag any role delegations that will require order-form amendments.
- Pricing impact: if your legal team wants a controller-carve (i.e., separate onshore-only processing), there will be an ops uplift. We estimate a recurring + one-time capacity surcharge — putting an initial estimate in Transfer_Addendum_Summary.pdf.

Can you confirm: 1) whether Evergreen needs an explicit transfer addendum executed as a separate exhibit, and 2) whether you need any certification evidence (SOC2, list of subprocessor regions) attached to the DPA?

Thanks — happy to set a 30m legal walkthrough this week.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

Attachments: Evergreen_DPA_markedup_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), Transfer_Addendum_Summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@evergreenhealth.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Thanks Naomi — reviewed briefly with in-house counsel. A few quick clarifications: 
1) Evergreen prefers the transfer addendum as a separate executed exhibit (helps our procurement reporting).
2) For evidence we need a SOC2 Type II attestation and a list of subprocessor hosting regions (we'll want to confirm EU-only routing where possible).
3) On roles: we expect a narrow processor role for hosting + inference; any training/model-tuning activities must be expressly excluded.

Legal would like to redline the DPA directly. Please confirm if you can accept a redline on the separate exhibit (we can share this by EOD). Also want a preliminary number for the one-time uplift so procurement can budget.

—Kim
Kimberly Huang
Senior Counsel, Evergreen Health
kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com

On Oct 1, 2026, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Kim — thanks for the call this morning....

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Looping in pricing/legal ops details per Kim's asks. Naomi — we can absorb SOC2 Type II evidence in the DPA exhibit (link + copy). On the uplift: preliminary breakouts below (ballpark):
- One-time migration/segmentation work: $18k–$26k (depends on VPC isolation level)
- Monthly reserved capacity surcharge: +12–18% on standard Dedicated throughput pricing (scales with token throughput).

We should avoid language that forces Redwood to be a 'controller' for any training work. Recommended redline bullets in the separate exhibit: 
- Explicit exclusion of model training/weight updates from processing scope.
- Affirmation that subprocessor list (live link) is sufficient evidence; provide last 30 days region footprint.

I can draft the pricing exhibit and a short SOW to attach to the order form — will send a first pass by EOD tomorrow.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Quick running notes after legal review — I'm attaching a short redline summary and proposed language for the transfer addendum. Key points we think will resolve: 
- Accept separate exhibit executed alongside the MSA (fine).
- Add a simple routing commitment: "Redwood will route EU-origin traffic to EU-hosted capacity by default; where EU-hosted capacity is not available, Redwood will notify and provide fallback options."
- Narrow the definitions: ensure 'processing' does not include ML model training unless a separate SOW is agreed.

Kim — can your legal team accept that routing commitment as operational (we prefer this than listing every subprocessor region)? If so, procurement can accept the separate exhibit and Ben's uplift estimate.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Lead, Contract Operations, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: transfer_addendum_proposed_language.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Thanks — that routing commitment looks acceptable in principle. A few requests from procurement/legal before we finalize: 
- Please include a short runbook: escalation contact, timeline for routing failover, and confirmation window for fallback notifications (we suggest 4 hours).
- For auditability, we need a clause that Redwood will provide a quarterly region footprint CSV for the last 90 days on request.

If you can incorporate those two items, Evergreen Legal will run a final redline and send formally. We'll plan for a 10/20 signature target if uplift estimate is confirmed this week.

—Kim

On Oct 5, 2026, Laura Bennett wrote:
> Quick running notes after legal review...

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Huang <kim.huang@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: GDPR transfer addendum, roles, and pricing impact

Kim — thanks, understood. We'll update the exhibit with: 1) a 4-hour fallback notification SLA and a short routing failover runbook; 2) quarterly region footprint CSV provision on request (non-sensitive summary only). Ben will circulate the updated pricing exhibit and SOW with the one-time uplift broken into line items by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps / owners: 
- Ben: send pricing exhibit + SOW (10/08)
- Laura: incorporate routing + runbook language into the transfer addendum (10/09)
- Naomi: consolidate final DPA bundle and coordinate signature lane (DocuSign link to follow)

If we stay on this cadence, we can meet the 10/20 go-live/signature target. Thanks all — I'll coordinate a 30m wrap-up call if Evergreen wants it.

—Naomi
